skill.name: icp-fit-scoring
skill.description: Score existing account or contact lists against your ideal customer profile using Leadsets company and role data. Review the evidence behind each score and sort prospects by fit.
skill.summary: Rank accounts and contacts by fit and see the evidence behind each score.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: One flag reflects an actual Leadsets connection that can transmit account and contact identifiers; the other 21 static flags are false positives. The workflow exports contact data by default without checking sharing permissions and can spend additional enrichment records when contacts have changed companies. No evidence found of prompt injection, shell execution, host reconnaissance, or environment access.

remediation.issue: Enrichment sends company and contact identifiers to Leadsets.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the recipient and fields before enrichment. Require approval to send contact identifiers and omit optional email or profile URLs unless needed.

remediation.issue: The default spreadsheet can retain work emails and other contact data without a sharing check.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the destination and authorized viewers before writing contact data. Omit work emails from exports unless the user requests them.

remediation.issue: Lookups for contacts who changed companies can exceed the planned record count.
remediation.suggestion: Set a per-run record cap and check the remaining budget before enriching any newly discovered domain. Pause for approval before exceeding the cap.

content.user_title: Score Accounts and Contacts for ICP Fit
content.value_statement: It is hard to prioritize sales lists when company details are missing and fit criteria are unclear. Use Leadsets data to score each prospect against your ideal customer profile and explain the result.
actual_capabilities: Turn a written ideal customer profile into weighted criteria and score tiers.
Normalize domains, remove duplicates before enrichment, and compare estimated usage with Leadsets quotas.
Retrieve industry, headcount band, location, and technology data when Leadsets provides those fields.
Score contacts by account and role fit, and flag contacts who have changed companies.
Assign scores from 0 to 100, explain each result, and separate rows with no data.
Export results to CSV or Google Sheets, or write them back through a connected spreadsheet or CRM.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and either a connected Leadsets MCP server or a REST API key.
Works only on an existing list. It does not find new prospects, scrape websites, or send outreach.
Missing criteria earn zero points. A lower score can reflect incomplete data rather than a mismatch.
Enrichment uses Leadsets records. Spreadsheet and CRM reads or writes require the relevant agent connection.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a founder's account list
use_cases.description: Rank an existing list of companies by industry, size, region, and technology before choosing which accounts to research first.

use_cases.title: Qualify webinar contacts
use_cases.description: Score registrants by employer fit and current role. Flag changes of employer before handing the list to sales.

use_cases.title: Review a CRM segment
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent scoring rubric to a CRM view. Export the tiers and keep accounts with no data separate for review.

prompt_templates.title: Score an account CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Score a short list with default weights.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score the attached CSV for US software companies with 51 to 200 employees that use HubSpot. Use default weights and explain every score. Export a new CSV.

prompt_templates.title: Rank contacts by account and role
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Combine account fit with contact seniority.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score the contacts in this sheet for Canadian software companies with 50 to 500 employees that use HubSpot. Target heads of sales and sales VPs. Flag contacts who changed employers and mark unknown criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Apply custom weights and tiers
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Rank a CRM segment using your own scoring rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score this CRM view for US software companies with 51 to 200 employees that use HubSpot. Weight industry and region at 35 each, headcount at 20, and technology at 10. Set A at 85, B at 65, and C at 45. Export a new CSV without changing the CRM.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a quota-limited scoring run
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review estimated usage and export access before enriching a large list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan scoring for these CRM contacts using our attached rubric. Count unique companies and contacts, then check the five-hour and weekly quotas. Before enrichment, show the batch plan and wait for approval of the record cap. Write the results to the approved sheet and omit work email.

output_examples.input: Score two accounts using the default weights for software, 51 to 200 employees, US location, and HubSpot.
output: Example Software: 80 of 100, tier A. Software, 51 to 200 employees, and HubSpot match. The company is in Canada, so it earns no region points.
Example Labs: No data. Leadsets found no company record, so this row is separate from No fit.

output_examples.input: Score a contact for a sales VP role. Use the default split of 60 points for account fit and 40 for role fit.
output: Example contact: 60 of 100, tier B. The current employer meets all account criteria, but the contact is a finance analyst, not a sales VP.
Employer change: flagged. Email status: unknown and unconfirmed. Email status did not affect the score.

best_practices: Define exact criteria, weights, and tier cutoffs before enrichment.
Review quota usage and approve a record cap before scoring a large list.
Confirm who can access the export and omit work emails unless they are needed.
anti_patterns: Treating missing information as evidence that a company does not fit.
Enriching the same company repeatedly for contacts who share a domain.
Treating catch-all or unknown email statuses as verified.

faq.question: What lists can I score?
faq.answer: Use a CSV, Google Sheet, or CRM view. Accounts need a company name or domain. Contacts need a name plus company or domain.

faq.question: Can I set my own scoring weights and tiers?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply weights and tier cutoffs with your profile. For contacts, the default is 60 points for account fit and 40 for role and seniority.

faq.question: How does missing data affect the score?
faq.answer: Missing criteria earn zero points and appear as unknown. Rows with no enrichment result go into No data rather than No fit.

faq.question: Does scoring consume Leadsets records?
faq.answer: The usage check is free. Each company or contact record returned by enrichment uses one record. The workflow checks quotas before the run.

faq.question: Where do the results go?
faq.answer: The default is a new Google Sheet with one tab per tier. You can request CSV export or writeback to a connected sheet or CRM.

faq.question: Does the skill contact prospects?
faq.answer: No. It scores existing records and reports email status when available. It does not send messages or enroll contacts in outreach sequences.
